title: Policy sweep A/B framework for dynamic batching & prefetch recommendations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an A/B experimentation framework that runs synchronous policy sweeps of batching and KV-prefetch configs, measures cost/latency/quality trade-offs per cohort, and wires safe automatic apply/rollback. This ticket scopes the experiment orchestration layer, metrics contract, and dashboarding needed for product teams to safely adopt automatic recommendations produced by the Optimize recommender service.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment service can run 5 concurrent config sweeps with isolated cohorts and traffic splits
Define canonical metric set (cost per request, p95 latency, quality regression) and expose them in a unified experiment API
Implement automated rollback triggers (error budget, quality drop >2%, latency SLO miss >10% p95) and prove via a canary run
Dashboard surfaces cohort-level time series, uplift vs control, and statistically meaningful confidence intervals (Bayesian/ROPE) for the primary metric
End-to-end demo: create a recommendation, run policy sweep, auto-apply winning config to 50% traffic with a staged rollout and automated monitoring guards
metrics: cost_per_1k_tokens: dollar cost normalized to 1000 input+output tokens
p95_latency_ms: 95th percentile latency to capture tail behavior
throughput_rps: successful requests per second in cohort
error_rate: percentage of requests returning 5xx or model-timeout
quality_regression_pct: percentage drop in evaluation pass rate on canonical prompt set
kv_cache_hit_rate: prefix/KV cache hit fraction for cohort
slo_breach_minutes: cumulative minutes per hour where latency SLO > threshold
dashboard_views: Cohort overview: side-by-side cards for control and each variant with cost, latency, quality, and trend sparklines
Time series with annotation layer: traffic splits, apply/rollback events, and release tag overlays
Uplift heatmap: metric delta as percent vs control across variants and models
Canary funnel: staged rollout funnel showing error signals and automatic holdpoints
Experiment summary: Bayesian posterior plot, ROPE zone, and recommended winner with credible interval
Config diff viewer: show exact batching/prefetch/kv settings applied per variant
rollout_plan: Step 1 - Preflight: static checks against binary compatibility and rollout whitelist (no private models)
Step 2 - Create experiment in the Experiment Service with N=3 variants (control + 2 policy sweeps)
Step 3 - Canary: route 1% traffic for 30m, monitor p95 and error_rate; automatic rollback triggers enabled
Step 4 - Staged rollout: if canary passes, expand to 10% for 2 hours, then 50% for 6 hours with automated metrics checks at each step
Step 5 - Full apply: 100% traffic with long-term observation and scheduled re-evaluation after 72h
Step 6 - Postmortem: collect telemetry, save experiment artifact, and publish recommendation to Optimize catalog
rollback_rules: Immediate rollback on error_rate > 0.5% absolute increase vs control during canary
Rollback if quality_regression_pct > 2% measured on the canonical eval set over the last 30 minutes
Hold and notify if p95_latency_ms increases by >10% relative to baseline for 10 consecutive minutes
Automatic rollback if anomaly detector flags sustained shift in token distribution or KV cache hit rate drops >15%
Manual override allowed via Console with audit log and operator confirmation
